title: The Gloom of Kilforth - (a brief) Take a Look
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ADwtKtLtE8Q

Daniel (@dungeondive) returns after four days of what he calls supernatural pain from a cracked molar and an exposed nerve. He has finally brought his Kickstarter copy of The Gloom of Kilforth to the table, and two games in he is completely won over. He says this is not a full review, just an overview while his enthusiasm is fresh. He also pushes back on its reputation as hard to learn: a few keywords are poorly explained, but it's nowhere near as convoluted as people claim.

The art comes first. Every card is a unique piece by Ania Kryczkowska, and he praises characters who are "beautiful but not over-sexualised" (a ninja dog among them). Then the systems. His half-elf wizard follows a four-chapter Saga that asks for cards with particular keywords: spell, enemy, title. Defeated encounters enter your hand as Rumours, which you must travel to a location to Discover before they become assets. Meanwhile, each night turns another region to its Gloom side and plot cards empower the boss.

He argues that direction from the Saga plus pressure from the plot cards tells a better story than Talisman, Runebound or Of Dreams & Shadows, and even ranks it above Fallout. He mentions Marco of Ward Gamer liked it without loving it, and says he disagrees.

----

Daniel says Kilforth hands you "great dots to connect" rather than a written story. Do you prefer games that script the narrative, or ones that leave you to join the dots?
